_comment: The real naked-eye sky, used as the chart's backdrop. Extracted from the HYG Database v4.4 (Hipparcos + Yale Bright Star + Gliese). Only direction, magnitude and colour index are kept — a backdrop needs no distances. Sol is excluded: it is the observer, not a background star, and at magnitude -26.7 it would swamp everything.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 — attribution required, and ShareAlike propagates to anything embedding this.
_display_limit: How faint a star the console will draw, which is not the same question as how faint a star was extracted. The chart fades a star by (7.0 - magnitude) / 5.2 and clamps that at 0.30, so every star fainter than magnitude 5.44 comes out at exactly the same alpha and exactly the same 1.1px square: the ramp has run out of room to tell them apart. The 2,065 stars past that point are not carrying magnitude any more, they are carrying uniform speckle across the systems the chart exists to show — and 40KB of it. The extract stays at 6.0 because that is what was taken from HYG and the number should not drift; the build cuts to this before shipping. Raise it back and the faint stars return, unchanged and still indistinguishable.
frame: Unit direction vectors in equatorial (ICRS) Cartesian, the same frame as systems.json.
packing: Flat int list, 5 per star: x*1000, y*1000, z*1000, mag*10, colour_index*100.
